*   Using only one auxiliary ray to approximate boundary motion (as in Loubet et al.) results in a biased estimator because the resulting warp field does not strictly satisfy the boundary requirement [S1, unofficial].

The claim states that using only one auxiliary ray to approximate boundary motion (as in Loubet et al.) results in a biased estimator because the resulting warp field does not strictly satisfy the boundary requirement. Source [S1] explicitly states in Section 2.3.2: 'Although the above approach successfully avoids sampling the discontinuities explicitly, it is biased due to the approximation of boundary’s motion using one of the auxiliary rays.' It further explains that the method by Loubet et al. constructs an 'imperfect warp field' that 'approximates (but does not strictly satisfy) requirement (b), or the boundary requirement.' Thus, every fact in the claim is present in the evidence.
supported
*   **When to use:** When unbiased differentiable rendering is required and explicit boundary sampling is difficult or biased [S1, unofficial].

The claim states that the method is used when unbiased differentiable rendering is required and explicit boundary sampling is difficult or biased. The evidence supports this in multiple ways: 1) It explicitly mentions that the auxiliary ray approximation approach (Loubet et al.) is 'biased' and that the proposed method (WAS) offers 'unbiased estimation'. 2) It states that the divergence theorem approach 'avoids explicit boundary sampling' by reparameterizing the integral. 3) It notes that this method enables advanced strategies like bidirectional path tracing, implying its utility in complex scenarios where explicit sampling might be difficult or insufficient.
supported
*   **Strengths:** Unbiased estimation; avoids explicit boundary sampling; enables multi-bounce transport estimation (via the path integral variant) [S1, unofficial].

The claim lists three specific attributes: 1) Unbiased estimation, 2) Avoids explicit boundary sampling, and 3) Enables multi-bounce transport estimation (via the path integral variant). Source [S1] explicitly states that Warped-Area Sampling (WAS) offers 'unbiased estimation' and 'avoids explicit boundary sampling' by reparameterizing the boundary integral into an interior integral. Furthermore, the source notes that an extension by Xu et al. applies this concept to the 'differential path integral,' which enables 'multi-bounce light transport estimation without explicit boundary sampling in path space.' All facts in the claim are directly supported by the provided text.
supported

It builds on [Reparametrized Integral Gradients](6785-reparametrized-integral-gradients.md) but improves upon the biased spherical rotation approach of Loubet et al. by satisfying the strict continuity requirements of the divergence theorem [S1, unofficial].

The claim states that the method builds on Reparametrized Integral Gradients (referenced as [6785-reparametrized-integral-gradients.md], which corresponds to the work by Loubet et al. [LHJ19] discussed in the text) and improves upon the biased spherical rotation approach of Loubet et al. by satisfying strict continuity requirements of the divergence theorem. Source [S1] explicitly states: 'The reparameterization using spherical rotation R proposed by Loubet et al. [LHJ19] can actually be interpreted as constructing an imperfect warp field V ... that approximates (but does not strictly satisfy) requirement (b), or the boundary requirement.' It further explains that the new method (WAS) constructs a warp field that satisfies the continuity requirements (a) and (b) required by the divergence theorem to avoid the bias present in Loubet's approach. Thus, all facts in the claim are present in the evidence.

An extension of WAS to differential path integrals by Xu et al. [XBLZ23], enabling multi-bounce light transport estimation without explicit boundary sampling in path space [S1, unofficial].

The claim states that Xu et al. [XBLZ23] extended WAS to differential path integrals, enabling multi-bounce light transport estimation without explicit boundary sampling in path space. The provided text explicitly confirms this in Section 2.3.3: 'To address this, Xu et al. [XBLZ23] introduce the idea of warped-area reparameterization to differential path integral... This means the interior integral and boundary integral in Eq. 12 can be composed into one interior integral, known as the reparameterized differential path integral... Compared to the reparameterized spherical integral in Eq. 32, the path integral in Eq. 36 has a more generalized form that depicts multi-bounce light transport within a scene.' The text also notes that the original WAS approach required repeated construction for single bounces, whereas the extension by Xu et al. operates on path space, avoiding explicit boundary sampling in that context.
